title: Aliasearch: research before reach-out
excerpt: I built a customer-research skill around one rule: a company name is not evidence. Find, verify, then decide what deserves a first message.
html:
A project note · customer research

Aliasearch

A research skill for finding people or organisations worth speaking to — with reasons, sources and enough context to make a real next decision.

See project on GitHub ↗

Most outreach problems are not writing problems. They are research problems hiding underneath.

Aliasearch grew from that frustration. Lists are easy to make; a useful list takes more care. A name from a directory, a fair listing or a search result may be a starting point, but it does not establish whether someone is real, relevant, reachable or worth interrupting.

So I turned the process into a reusable skill: give it a real offer, a market, a target and a standard of proof. It finds candidates from appropriate public sources, keeps the evidence close, and only prepares a draft when there is a sensible case for it.

How it works

01 / BRIEF

Start with what matters.

Offer, audience, market, exclusions, desired count and evidence bar.

02 / DISCOVER

Search where signal lives.

Directories, associations, trade lists, company sites and accessible public profiles.

03 / VERIFY

Separate names from fit.

Normalize duplicates, check claims, preserve source context and mark uncertainty.

04 / DECIDE

Make next step easier.

Return a lean, reviewable list and draft a tailored message only when asked.

Four gates before a first message

IdentityIs this a real person or organisation in the requested market?
Role or needIs there evidence they buy, resell or experience the problem in question?
Offer fitDoes their work connect to the actual product or use case?
Public routeIs there a credible public route to contact them, with evidence attached?

What I wanted to protect

Aliasearch should not turn uncertainty into confidence theatre. It keeps candidates separate from qualified prospects, labels missing proof and does not pad results just to hit a requested count. The useful outcome is not a giant spreadsheet. It is a smaller set of people or organisations a human can review with confidence.

Human judgement stays in loop.

Aliasearch does not send messages, promise internet-wide coverage or claim reply rates. It helps make a better researched decision; a person still decides whether, when and how to reach out.

Why I care about it

I like systems that make careful work easier to repeat. Aliasearch is early, but that is the direction: research that is practical enough to use, honest enough to trust, and structured enough to improve after every real run.

If you build, sell or research and have thoughts on where this breaks, I would genuinely like to hear them.
